definition: In mathematical optimization, the network simplex algorithm is a graph theoretic specialization of the simplex algorithm.
details: The algorithm is usually formulated in terms of a minimum-cost flow problem. The network simplex method works very well in practice, typically 200 to 300 times faster than the simplex method applied to general linear program of same dimensions.

explainer.lead: The network simplex algorithm is a graph-theoretic specialization of the simplex algorithm in mathematical optimization. It is usually formulated as a minimum-cost flow problem and typically runs 200 to 300 times faster than the general simplex method on problems of the same dimensions.

tiers.eli5: It is a shortcut route-finding method for sending things through a network at the lowest cost, much quicker than the general-purpose method.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers formulate minimum-cost flow problems and solve them with network simplex for its speed in practice. Its speed advantage is tied to the network structure of the problem.
tiers.paperLevel: A graph-theoretic specialization of the simplex algorithm, usually formulated as a minimum-cost flow problem; typically 200 to 300 times faster than the simplex method on a general linear program of the same dimensions.

explainer.example: A minimum-cost flow problem is solved with network simplex instead of general simplex, running roughly 200 to 300 times faster at the same dimensions.
